title: Bug Record v1
description: One record per bug, appended once — no event stream, no fold (v0.5.0 FR2, D11, AR-1). Each line of specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl is one object validating this schema, keyed by `id`. Every property carries a custom `x-mutability` keyword — `immutable-core` (never rewritten through the record-store update seam once appended), `write-once` (legitimately absent from a freshly registered record; settable exactly once from absent, then immutable), or `mutable-governance` (rewritten in place through the atomic in-place update seam, `core/atomic_write.py` + refuse-stale) — THIS is the one place the three-category split is declared; bugs.py reads it from here. bugs.py refuses a write carrying a value the push would refuse; it never rewrites one. 0.4.7 FR1 retired the seven derived-provenance keys (lineage_source, registration_commit/_granularity, resolved_commit/resolution_granularity, root_cause, migration_note): a git-derived cache stored in the record. `additionalProperties: false` refuses them. `status` has NO `picked` value (v0.5.0 FR2): the pick is the bundled definition commit, readable by pillar 2 (FR8 shape 5).

id.description: Stable identifier of this bug (kebab-case slug) — the record store's key.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the record was first appended (registration time).

reported_by.description: Agent or runtime that registered this record.

surface.description: The directory of the context's own repo whose tooling broke — one name matching ^[a-z0-9_-]+$, tracked at any depth (F011); `bugs.py append` refuses anything else. Records born before carry free text or the legacy `unknown`, valid as written.

correlates.description: The ledger ids this bug was judged to correlate with at registration, empty for none (ADR 0127); absent on records born before it.

component.description: Free text: the `path#symbol` precision the fine-key analysis needs (component stays free text — only `surface` closed).

context.description: The active spec-context the bug was found in.

repro.description: The exact command / steps to reproduce.

status.description: Governance state. NO `picked` value (v0.5.0 FR2) — the pick is the bundled definition commit, not a status.

cause.description: The one generic mutable-governance narrative field, reused across transitions rather than a second field per verb: the fix's statement of what caused the bug when resolved, or the reason narrative when deferred/rejected.

caused_by.description: The prior bug id this one was caused by, when this record is itself a reopen (a new id declaring `caused_by`).

resolved_release.description: The release id that shipped the fix.

audited.description: The audit window id that reviewed this resolution — written by the auditor through the one governance-update seam, in a single atomic rewrite (FR14 pillar 1).

closed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant this record reached a terminal status; null while status is 'open' (0.4.7 FR4). Stamped by the four terminal transitions and by nothing else (bugs.py), unreachable through `bugs.py update` for the same reason 'status' is. `bugs.py archive` and SPEC-DOC-041 age by THIS field, never by `ts` — `ts` is the FILING date, so a bug filed long ago and closed yesterday used to be archivable the day it closed. Never earlier than `ts` (LEDGER-BUGS-SCHEMA refuses closed_at < ts), and non-null if and only if `status` is terminal.

solution.description: Absent until the fix lands; immutable the moment it is written.

evidence_loop.description: The FR23 evidence triple, restored (v0.4.4, not re-invented): the red-loop command that reproduced the bug on the executed path, before any hypothesis.

evidence_seam.description: The FR23 evidence triple: the test file/node (the regression seam) that pins the fix.

evidence_diff.description: The FR23 evidence triple: the diff direction on the touched feature, prefixed 'net-negative:'/'net-positive:'/'net-neutral:' with a checkable rationale.

superseded_by.description: The backlog/bug/release slug that supersedes this record — required when `status` is `superseded`; a sweep closure takes this status, never `resolved` (FR2).
